module purpose: The watchdog block accepts bus configuration and reload requests, runs a prescaled counter when enabled, compares the counter against a programmable timeout and, on timeout or forced-access conditions, asserts a hardware reset output; it also reports control fields and the reset cause on the bus and exports a clock-enable signal.

use-case flows.value: Control register fields (enable, lock, strict, timeout) written into internal ctrl record by bus writes to the control address
Watchdog reload / clear request (reset_wdt) set by a bus write of the correct password
Prescaler tick (from clkgen_i) drives cnt_started and increments cnt; when cnt equals ctrl.timeout (cnt_timeout) hw_rst_timeout is produced
Readback of control fields and reset cause returned on bus reads into bus_rsp_o.data
The lock bit freezes control writes (attempts to write while locked cause reset_force)
System reset output rstn_o asserted when hw_rst_timeout or hw_rst_access are set; reset_cause captured accordingly

conceptual assets.concept: Watchdog enable configuration (whether the WDT is enabled and the exported clock-enable)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The enable bit is written by bus writes into ctrl.enable (assignment at RTL line 94) and is stored in a clocked register (map: ctrl.enable occurrence 3 CLOCKED_BY clk_i). The WDT counting logic depends on this bit (cnt_started and cnt updates at lines 129-135) and hw_rst_timeout uses it (line 155). The same setting is exported outside the block as clkgen_en_o (assignment at line 140; map: clkgen_en_o occurrence 2 COPIES ctrl.enable). Therefore the module's counting behavior and the external clock-enable it drives depend on the integrity of ctrl.enable.

conceptual assets.concept: Configuration lock (whether control fields are frozen against writes)
conceptual assets.reasoning: ctrl.lock determines whether writes to the control register are accepted: bus_access checks ctrl.lock and, if it is '1', sets reset_force instead of updating control fields (RTL lines 93 and 99). ctrl.lock is itself a clocked register written at line 95 (map: ctrl.lock occurrence 4 CLOCKED_BY clk_i). Thus the module's acceptance or rejection of remote configuration writes depends on the integrity of ctrl.lock.

conceptual assets.concept: Timeout setting (the programmable timeout value the counter is compared against)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The timeout field is written into ctrl.timeout from bus data (assignment at RTL line 97) and is held in a clocked register (map: ctrl.timeout occurrence 3 CLOCKED_BY clk_i). The equality cnt = ctrl.timeout produces cnt_timeout (line 144) which is used to generate hw_rst_timeout (line 155). Therefore the timeout value's integrity determines when a timeout-based reset will occur.

conceptual assets.concept: Strict mode configuration (whether forced-access generates a hardware reset)
conceptual assets.reasoning: ctrl.strict is written from bus data into a clocked register (RTL line 96; map: ctrl.strict occurrence 3 CLOCKED_BY clk_i) and is used together with ctrl.enable and reset_force to produce hw_rst_access (RTL line 156). The integrity of ctrl.strict therefore determines whether an access that sets reset_force will result in a system reset.

conceptual assets.concept: Watchdog reload request (the reload/clear signal that resets the WDT counter)
conceptual assets.reasoning: A bus write with the correct password sets reset_wdt <= '1' (RTL lines 101-104) and reset_wdt is clocked into a register (map: reset_wdt occurrence 4 CLOCKED_BY clk_i). wdt_counter uses reset_wdt to clear cnt (lines 131-133). The integrity of reset_wdt therefore controls whether the counter is reloaded/cleared and so affects timeout availability.

conceptual assets.concept: Forced-reset indicator (reset_force) set on disallowed or incorrect bus accesses
conceptual assets.reasoning: reset_force is set by the bus-access logic on writes that are disallowed (writes while ctrl.lock = '1' or wrong password writes) (RTL lines 99 and 105) and is stored in a clocked register (map: reset_force occurrence 5 CLOCKED_BY clk_i). reset_force participates in producing hw_rst_access (RTL line 156). Thus integrity of reset_force determines whether an invalid access is escalated to a hardware reset.

conceptual assets.concept: Watchdog counter state (current counter value used to detect timeout)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The cnt register holds the running watchdog count (wdt_counter updates at lines 129-135) and is clocked (map: cnt occurrence 4 CLOCKED_BY clk_i). When cnt equals ctrl.timeout the combinational cnt_timeout becomes '1' (line 144) which leads to hw_rst_timeout (line 155). The integrity of cnt therefore directly determines when a timeout-based reset is triggered.

conceptual assets.concept: Counter-started flag (whether the watchdog counter is active)
conceptual assets.reasoning: cnt_started is set from ctrl.enable and prescaler activity (wdt_counter lines 129-131) and is stored (map: cnt_started occurrence 4 CLOCKED_BY clk_i). cnt_started gates counter increments and the timeout condition (lines 129 and 144), so its integrity affects whether the WDT actually advances toward a timeout.

conceptual assets.concept: Reset cause register (the recorded source of the last reset)
conceptual assets.reasoning: reset_cause is set by the reset_identifier process to indicate external debug reset, timeout, or forced-access (RTL lines 171-176) and is stored in a clocked register (map: reset_cause occurrence 4 CLOCKED_BY clk_i). The value is returned on bus reads (copied into bus_rsp_o.data at line 111), so the integrity of reset_cause is required for correct reporting of why a reset occurred.

conceptual assets.concept: System reset output (the rstn_o value derived from internal reset flags)
conceptual assets.reasoning: The block drives rstn_o from the internal reset flags (rstn_o <= not (hw_rst_timeout or hw_rst_access), RTL line 161; map: rstn_o occurrence 2 DERIVES_FROM hw_rst_access and hw_rst_timeout). The internal flags hw_rst_timeout and hw_rst_access are produced by reset_generator (lines 155-156) and are stored in clocked registers (map: hw_rst_timeout occurrence 3 CLOCKED_BY clk_i; hw_rst_access occurrence 3 CLOCKED_BY clk_i). The integrity of those stored decisions and the derived rstn_o output is therefore established by the RTL: corrupting them changes the reset delivered to the system.
